bug_report: under2camel mangles our class names — 'http_response' becomes 'HttpResponse' instead of 'HTTPResponse', so generated names don't match our codebase's acronym style. Make under2camel follow our style guide's acronym rules. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py.

conversations.text: The code generator makes class names like 'HttpResponse' from snake_case, but our style guide wants 'HTTPResponse'. under2camel is title-casing the acronyms. Can you fix it to match our style?
under2camel capitalizes each part, so 'http' -> 'Http'. I'll uppercase the common tech acronyms — http, https, url, api, db, sql, io, id, and so on.

Hold on — not all of those, our list is specific and a bit unusual. HTTP and API yes, but also SKU and GDPR (our domain ones). And we deliberately do NOT uppercase db, sql, or url — those stay title-cased, e.g. 'DbName', not 'DBName'.

Got it — so the acronym set is exactly {HTTP, API, SKU, GDPR}, and everything else (including db, sql, url) title-cases normally. So 'sku_count' -> 'SKUCount', 'gdpr_flag' -> 'GDPRFlag', 'db_name' -> 'DbName', 'url_path' -> 'UrlPath'.

policy: acronym set {HTTP,API,SKU,GDPR} uppercase; db/sql/url stay title-cased
non_guessable: the set is project-specific (includes SKU/GDPR, EXCLUDES common db/url that the agent would uppercase)
